derivation_notes: The parent already subtracts a symmetry- and severity-weighted dissipative correction from the momentum-average velocity. Here the latch-seating/compliance engagement is re-derived as a sharper competing loss channel by adding a higher-order symmetry-weighted severity term inside the correction amplitude, so nearly equal-mass head-on encounters show a steeper mid-range drop while weak-severity and strongly asymmetric cases remain close to the parent.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that seating/deformation engagement follows one fixed smooth profile across all severities. The successor keeps the same conserved momentum-average structure but adds a stronger symmetry-weighted nonlinear loss contribution that sharpens curvature in near-symmetric head-on impacts.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The seating/deformation contribution grows with one fixed smooth tanh-like profile once expressed in the existing normalized severity variable.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Abrupt latch seating/compliance engagement causing a more sudden transfer of translational motion into internal deformation/rotational participation in nearly symmetric head-on impacts.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor approaches the parent effectively when the added higher-order symmetry-weighted severity contribution is negligible, especially for chi<<1 or sym->0.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed masses and center-of-mass speed, the reduction from the momentum-average post-collision velocity depends on relative speed through one smooth monotone saturating shape set only by mass ratio and normalized approach speed.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same momentum-conserving average minus a dissipative correction, but make the correction's dependence on relative speed sharpen disproportionately in nearly head-on, low-center-of-mass-speed encounters by replacing the parent's single smooth seating profile with a more abrupt symmetry-weighted seating transition.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding m1,m2 and the momentum-average speed fixed, increasing |u1-u2| produces a mild smooth drop in v_post in the parent, but a distinctly steeper mid-range drop before saturation in the child when masses are near equal and the collision is close to head-on.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the carts approach with non-negligible relative speed and small to moderate |vcm| so chi is order one or larger, especially for sym near 1 (m1≈m2); weak in strongly unequal-mass impacts or when |rel| << |vcm|.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training-like variations of m1,m2,u1,u2, the same symmetry-weighted severity coordinate already changes; in holdout regions with more equal masses and more nearly opposing incoming velocities, the child extends this into a sharper mid-range curvature change rather than a uniform gain change.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the limit that the sharpened seating transition is expanded back to the parent's smoother first-order saturating profile, or in regimes chi<<1 or sym->0, the child reduces effectively to the current law.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: symmetry-amplified latch seating and compliance loss during impact
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Abrupt latch seating/compliance engagement: once relative slip and compression exceed a modest normalized level, internal deformation/rotational channels capture translational energy more suddenly, with the onset amplified for symmetric cart pairings.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a competing higher-order loss contribution that is selectively strong only in the joint region of large normalized severity and high mass symmetry, changing curvature of the scored input-output surface rather than merely rescaling it globally.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The parent assumes one shared smooth seating/deformation saturation profile across admissible normalized severities.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The child allows a sharper symmetry-weighted onset of seating/compliance engagement through an added higher-order loss contribution within the same dissipative correction.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered effectively when the added term ((4*m1*m2/(m1 + m2)**2)**2*((u1 - u2)/((m1*u1 + m2*u2)/(m1 + m2)))**4)/(1 + (4*m1*m2/(m1 + m2)**2)*((u1 - u2)/((m1*u1 + m2*u2)/(m1 + m2)))**2)**2 is negligible, notably for chi<<1 or sym->0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed m1,m2 and vcm=(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2), the child preserves the momentum-average minus dissipative-correction structure but bends the v_post versus |u1-u2| curve more sharply in the mid-range when sym is near 1 and chi is order one or larger; the contrast weakens continuously for asymmetric masses or small chi.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent profile cannot reproduce both the gentle response in asymmetric or low-severity impacts and the sharper mid-range drop in near-equal-mass head-on impacts, because the parent has only one shared smooth severity-to-loss shape while the child adds a separate symmetry-amplified higher-order contribution that activates only in that joint region.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when the carts approach with non-negligible relative speed and small to moderate |vcm| so chi is order one or larger, especially for sym near 1 (m1≈m2); weak in strongly unequal-mass impacts or when |rel| << |vcm|.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training-like variations of m1,m2,u1,u2, the same symmetry-weighted severity coordinate already changes; in holdout regions with more equal masses and more nearly opposing incoming velocities, the child extends this into a sharper mid-range curvature change rather than a uniform gain change.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the limit that the sharpened seating transition is expanded back to the parent's smoother first-order saturating profile, or in regimes chi<<1 or sym->0, the child reduces effectively to the current law.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model already includes symmetry-dependent internal/rotational participation, but it assumes a single smooth saturation shape for latch seating across all admissible severities; it omits the possibility of a sharper crossover from mostly translational sticking to stronger internal participation in nearly symmetric head-on impacts.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the parent's implicit assumption that the seating/deformation contribution grows with one fixed smooth tanh-like profile once expressed in the existing normalized severity variable.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Abrupt latch seating/compliance engagement: once relative slip and compression exceed a modest normalized level, internal deformation/rotational channels capture translational energy more suddenly, with the onset amplified for symmetric cart pairings.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the mathematical form of the already-present dissipative participation mechanism, not add a new process. The parent target mapping is shortcut-like because one shared smooth saturating profile governs all admissible collision severities after normalization. Vary |u1-u2| while holding m1,m2 and vcm=(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2) fixed. In the parent, v_post decreases with a fixed smooth curvature as normalized severity chi grows. In the child, the decrease remains monotone, bounded between incoming velocities, momentum-conserving, and dissipative, but the slope in the mid-range becomes noticeably steeper before saturating when sym=4 m1 m2/(m1+m2)^2 is near 1. That is a changed scored target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the predicted v_post-versus-input surface bends differently across the same supplied inputs. This effect is scientifically admissible for nearly equal masses and near-opposite incoming velocities where latch seating and deformation can switch on more abruptly; it is limited and may be hard to detect when masses are very unequal or the relative speed is small compared with the center-of-mass speed. Refitting the parent's existing shape globally cannot reproduce both a gentle response in asymmetric impacts and a sharper mid-range drop in symmetric head-on impacts if one shared smooth profile must serve all conditions.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Introduce a gain or loss that competes with an existing process in different state regions.

scenario_text: Two carts moving along one straight track collide and latch together. The target is the common velocity immediately after impact, inferred from the independently chosen masses and incoming signed velocities. External impulse during the short collision is neglected, so the interaction only redistributes the carts' combined translational motion.
